proof:
Context. This child is the measurability preliminaries (P1), (P1'), (P2), (P3) and (P4) of the proof of gwe_varifold_graph_transfer. Only continuity of f on B is used. In the parent, f is 1-Lipschitz on B, hence continuous there (LipschitzOnWith.continuousOn). The Lean proof may add the pinned import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Polish.Basic (Lusin-Souslin), as accepted siblings did.

Notation. B := closedBall (0 : R^n) R and F(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)) for x in R^n.

1. Continuity of graphPoint. By definition graphPoint a b = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.append (ofLp a) (ofLp b)), so its coordinate of index i is Fin.append (ofLp a) (ofLp b) i (PiLp.toLp_apply).
 - Every i in Fin (n + l) is Fin.castAdd l j for some j in Fin n, or Fin.natAdd n k for some k in Fin l (Fin.addCases).
 - In the first case the coordinate is a_j (Fin.append_left); in the second it is b_k (Fin.append_right).
 - So every coordinate of (a, b) |-> graphPoint a b is a coordinate projection of a or of b, hence continuous on R^n x R^l (PiLp.continuous_apply composed with continuous_fst or continuous_snd).
 - A map into R^{n+l} = PiLp 2 (fun _ => R) is continuous when all its coordinates are (continuous_pi, PiLp.continuous_toLp). Hence (a, b) |-> graphPoint a b is continuous.
2. (P1) F is continuous on B. The map x |-> (x, f x) is continuous on B because f is (ContinuousOn.prodMk with continuousOn_id). Compose with the continuous map of step 1 and the continuous isometry q.
3. (P1') F is injective on all of R^n. If F x = F y, then graphPoint x (f x) = graphPoint y (f y) because q is injective. By step 1, the coordinates of index Fin.castAdd l j give x_j = y_j for every j in Fin n. Hence x = y.
4. Proof of (i) (P2). Let A be a Borel subset of B.
 - graphOver f A = (x |-> graphPoint x (f x)) '' A, so q '' graphOver f A = F '' A (Set.image_image).
 - F is continuous on A (step 2, A ⊆ B; ContinuousOn.mono) and injective on A (step 3).
 - R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) is a Polish space (complete, separable, metrizable) with its Borel sigma-algebra. R^{n+l} is Hausdorff with its Borel sigma-algebra.
 - By the Lusin-Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), F '' A is Borel.
5. Proof of (ii) (P3). Let Fh := B.piecewise F (fun _ => 0); membership in B is decided classically. So Fh(x) = F(x) for x in B and Fh(x) = 0 otherwise.
 - F is continuous on B (step 2), and the constant map 0 is continuous on the complement of B.
 - B is closed, hence Borel (measurableSet_closedBall).
 - By ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, Fh is Borel. For x in B, Fh(x) = F(x) (Set.piecewise_eq_of_mem).
6. Proof of (iii) (P4).
 - For every f, the map x |-> fderiv R f x from R^n to R^n →L[R] R^l (with its Borel sigma-algebra) is Borel (measurable_fderiv; R^l is complete).
 - Define Phi(D) := sqrt(det(I_n + (<D e_a, D e_b>)_{a,b})) for D in R^n →L[R] R^l.
 - For fixed a, b, the entry D |-> <D e_a, D e_b> is continuous: evaluation at a fixed vector is continuous (continuous_eval_const) and the inner product is jointly continuous (Continuous.inner).
 - Hence D |-> (<D e_a, D e_b>)_{a,b} is continuous into n x n matrices (continuous_matrix, after Matrix.of_apply). Adding the constant identity matrix is continuous, det is continuous (Continuous.matrix_det), and sqrt is continuous (Real.continuous_sqrt).
 - So Phi is continuous, hence Borel (Continuous.measurable), and J_f = Phi o (fderiv R f) is Borel as a composition of Borel maps. QED
key_steps: (a, b) |-> graphPoint a b is continuous coordinatewise (Fin.append_left/right), so F = q(graphPoint x (f x)) is continuous on B.
F is injective: the coordinates of graphPoint x (f x) of index Fin.castAdd l j are x_j.
Lusin-Souslin (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn) with q '' graphOver f A = F '' A gives (i).
Fh := B.piecewise F 0 is Borel (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, B closed) and equals F on B.
J_f = Phi o fderiv R f, with Phi continuous (continuous_matrix, Continuous.matrix_det, Real.continuous_sqrt) and fderiv R f Borel (measurable_fderiv).
